cross_field_relationships.description: Geometric definition of trigonometric parallax. Distance in parsecs is inversely proportional to parallax in milliarcseconds: d[pc] = 1000 / π[mas]. This is a strict mathematical conversion derived from baseline geometry, though measurement noise can produce unphysical negative values.

Parallax measures geometric distance via annual stellar motion, while [Fe/H] quantifies photospheric chemical composition. These are independent stellar properties with no direct physical coupling or deterministic law linking them.

Distance indicates spatial location within the Galactic gravitational potential, whereas metallicity reflects nucleosynthetic history and local interstellar medium enrichment. No direct physical law couples them for individual stars.

Parallax is a geometric distance indicator, while pulsation period is governed by the star's mean density, mass, and internal opacity structure (κ-mechanism). They are independent observables, though jointly utilized to anchor the Cepheid Period-Luminosity relation.

Distance is a geometric property, while pulsation period depends on stellar radius, mass, and evolutionary state. Although the Period-Luminosity relation empirically links period to intrinsic brightness, it does not physically dictate or constrain the star's distance.

Treat Gaia-derived [Fe/H] and m_h as qualitative indicators unless cross-validated with high-resolution spectroscopy
